subject: Deep Slice Explorer: action plan and telemetry asks
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Ramirez <alicia@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Wed, 23 May 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Deep Slice Explorer: action plan and telemetry asks

Ben / Marissa —

Following the call with Alicia (Nimbus) this morning, they reiterated the need for a lightweight per-route exploration tool that lets them:
- surface cost/latency outliers by tenant and route slice
- pivot from an anomalous token path to the raw trace and the example request
- see a 30/90 day delta and quickly pin the causal model variant or rollout that coincided with the change

I sketched a minimal proposal (attached) that is a phased implementation:
Phase 1 (MVP): per-route cost + p95/p99 latency heatmap, link to trace id, and a runbook link per anomaly.
Phase 2: sample playback for single requests and a small in-console query builder for slice filters.

Telemetry asks in the doc (short):
- include route_id, model_variant, tenant_id, batch_size, token_count, kv_cache_hit, and trace_id in the token-path records
- add a boolean "was_cached_prefix" flag on request completion rows
- expose sample-level payload (redacted) via trace links for the example playback feature

Can you confirm technical feasibility for Phase 1 within a 3-sprint window and whether we need any schema migration on the ingestion side? Also calling out that Nimbus expects the initial prototype to include cost attribution by quantized model variant (they run mixed-precision + quantized backends).

I've attached a short spec and a screenshot from Nimbus to illustrate the pain. I'm happy to take this into the Product/UX kickoff if we agree on scope.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: deep_slice_specs.pdf (4 pages), sample-heatmap-2028-05-22.png

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Ramirez <alicia@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Wed, 23 May 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deep Slice Explorer: action plan and telemetry asks

Thanks Sofia — this looks sensible and aligns with a lot of ops asks we've seen. A few quick clarifying questions before I scope: 
1) For the cost attribution by model_variant: do we have precise model_variant tagging in the serving runtime today or would this require adding a variant label at request time?
2) For the trace link, do you want a pre-signed ephemeral link to the trace playback (90d TTL) or a pointer to internal replay that requires auth? Nimbus prefers an exportable sample for internal audits.
3) On sampling: Phase 1, do we accept a 1% sample for traceable requests or is Nimbus expecting full-fidelity for any detected anomaly?

From an infra side, if we can get the token-paths to include model_variant and kv_cache_hit, I think we can stitch cost attribution without a schema migration (we already store model_name + precision in the token-profile), but I need to confirm that model_variant (for multi-rollout) is emitted. I'll check with runtime team today.

Tentative ask: assuming minimal ingestion changes, I can get an MVP frontend backed by a precomputed heatmap index + trace links in two sprints. If we need schema changes we'll add a sprint for ingestion work.

Ben
Ben Carter
Observability / Instrumentation
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 May 2028 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deep Slice Explorer: action plan and telemetry asks

Looping in product scope decisions:
- I agree with Phase 1 being heatmap + trace link + runbook anchor. That gives customers immediate value (detect -> investigate -> mitigation).
- Priority = P1 for Nimbus (they're a renewal opportunity and are actively seeing tail-cost regressions).

Deliverable schedule proposal:
- Week 1 (sprint A): Ben to validate runtime emits model_variant and kv_cache_hit. If missing, runtime to add a small header so ingestion can tag token-paths.
- Week 2 (sprint B): Ingestion team to add 2 fields to token-path schema + backfill 7 days for demo if feasible.
- Week 3 (sprint B): Frontend MVP with heatmap and trace links, internal QA.
- Week 4 (sprint C): Customer demo + feedback loop and runbook population.

Marissa to own customer demo deck and acceptance criteria. Sofia to own feature spec and runbook templates. Ben to own instrumentation and front-end prototype.

Marissa Cole
Director, Product — Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Alicia Ramirez <alicia@nimbushealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 May 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deep Slice Explorer: action plan and telemetry asks

Thanks all — this matches what we discussed. A couple of notes from Nimbus: 
- For audits we need an exportable CSV of the sample-level payload (redacted PII) for any anomaly date range. If you can expose an export from the trace link that would be ideal.
- We can tolerate 5% sampling for proactive dashboards, but for any anomaly we expect the system to be able to surface the full set of requests in the incident window (we'll accept a best-effort 24h backfill if needed).
- Model variant tagging is a must for us — our mixed-precision rollout was the root cause in a recent incident.

Happy to join the Week 4 demo and provide concrete payload examples.

— Alicia Ramirez
Head of Platform Engineering, Nimbus Health
